## Solution

Let $q = e^{-\pi}$, so that $\sinh(n\pi) = \frac{q^{-n}-q^n}{2}$, giving

$$\frac{1}{\sinh(n\pi)} = \frac{2q^n}{1-q^{2n}} = 2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} q^{(2j+1)n}.$$

Therefore

$$S = \sum_{\substack{n\ge1\\n\text{ odd}}} \frac{1}{n}\cdot 2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} q^{(2j+1)n} = 2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\sum_{\substack{n\ge1\\n\text{ odd}}}\frac{(q^{2j+1})^{n}}{n}.$$

Using the odd-part of the Taylor series $-\ln(1-x)$:

$$\sum_{\substack{n\ge1\\n\text{ odd}}}\frac{x^n}{n} = \operatorname{arctanh}(x) = \tfrac12\ln\frac{1+x}{1-x},$$

we get

$$S = 2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+q^{2j+1}}{1-q^{2j+1}} = \ln\prod_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{1+q^{2j+1}}{1-q^{2j+1}}.$$

### Reducing to theta functions

The Jacobi triple-product gives, with nome $q$:

$$\vartheta_3(0\,|\,q)=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{2n})(1+q^{2n-1})^2,\qquad \vartheta_4(0\,|\,q)=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{2n})(1-q^{2n-1})^2.$$

Hence

$$\sqrt{\frac{\vartheta_3(0\,|\,q)}{\vartheta_4(0\,|\,q)}} = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1+q^{2n-1}}{1-q^{2n-1}},$$

and so

$$S = \tfrac12\ln\frac{\vartheta_3(0\,|\,q)}{\vartheta_4(0\,|\,q)}.$$

### Special value at $q = e^{-\pi}$ (i.e. $\tau = i$)

The elliptic modulus and complementary modulus are

$$k = \frac{\vartheta_2^2(0\,|\,q)}{\vartheta_3^2(0\,|\,q)},\qquad k' = \frac{\vartheta_4^2(0\,|\,q)}{\vartheta_3^2(0\,|\,q)},$$

with the nome relation $q = e^{-\pi K'(k)/K(k)}$, i.e. $\tau = i\,K'(k)/K(k)$.

At $\tau = i$ we have $K'(k)/K(k)=1$, so $K(k')=K(k)$. Since $k^2+k'^2=1$, this forces $k=k'=1/\sqrt2$ (the lemniscatic case). Therefore

$$\frac{\vartheta_4^2(0\,|\,e^{-\pi})}{\vartheta_3^2(0\,|\,e^{-\pi})} = k' = \frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad \frac{\vartheta_3(0\,|\,e^{-\pi})}{\vartheta_4(0\,|\,e^{-\pi})} = 2^{1/4}.$$

### Final computation

$$S = \tfrac12\ln\!\bigl(2^{1/4}\bigr) = \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac14\ln 2 = \frac{\ln 2}{8}.$$

Hence

$$\boxed{8S = \ln 2}.$$

**Numerical check.** $\sinh\pi\approx 11.5487$, so the $n=1$ term is $\approx 0.08659$; the $n=3$ term is $\approx 5.4\times10^{-5}$, giving $S\approx 0.08664$. Meanwhile $\ln 2/8\approx 0.693147/8\approx 0.086643$. The values agree. $\blacksquare$

So $S = \ln\sqrt{\vartheta_3/\vartheta_4} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(\vartheta_3/\vartheta_4)$.
